title: A boolean must be compared with true to be used as a condition
statement: A boolean variable or expression cannot be used directly as a condition; it has to be compared with true or false first, and a comparison is the only thing that produces a condition.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: write a condition from a boolean variable
evidence_patterns.signature: writes == true (or == True) and cannot explain what if done: alone would do

example.item: done is a boolean. Write the condition for 'if done'.

evidence_patterns.notes: The == True form runs correctly, so this is only diagnosable by asking, or from a follow-up item.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: return a boolean from a comparison
evidence_patterns.signature: wraps the comparison in if/else returning literal true and false

discriminators.vs_slip: A slip is a stylistic habit the learner can drop when asked. The belief is the claim that if done: is invalid or that a comparison is not a value.

conflicts_with.label: A boolean expression is itself a value

resolved_by.label: A boolean expression is itself a value
